title: Ensure any change to code receives approval of two strongly authenticated users
description: Ensure that every code change is reviewed and approved by two authorized contributors who are both strongly authenticated - using Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA), from the team relevant to the code change. To prevent malicious or unauthorized code changes, the first layer of protection is the process of code review. This process involves engineer teammates reviewing each other's code for errors, optimizations, and general ... Checks the default branch: a pull request with at least 2 approving reviews is required. Satisfied by classic branch protection or an active ruleset (rules/branches). Uses the GitHub REST/GraphQL API through gh api (read-only). The repository comes from GH_REPO or the current git checkout (gh's {owner}/{repo} resolution, GH_HOST for GitHub Enterprise Server); the organization comes from GH_ORG (default: the repository owner). Fails when gh is missing or unauthenticated (gh auth login or GH_TOKEN); organization settings and branch protection need an owner/admin token.
reference: CIS GitHub Benchmark v1.2.0 - 1.1.3 Ensure any change to code receives approval of two strongly authenticated users

audit.command:
command -v gh >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1
gh auth status >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1
info=$(gh api 'repos/{owner}/{repo}' --jq '.full_name + " " + .default_branch' 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
R=${info% *}; B=${info#* }
[ -n "$R" ] && [ -n "$B" ] || exit 1
p=$(gh api "repos/$R/branches/$B/protection" --jq '(.required_pull_request_reviews.required_approving_review_count // 0) >= 2' 2>/dev/null) || p=false
s=$(gh api "repos/$R/rules/branches/$B" --jq 'any(.[]; .type == "pull_request" and (.parameters.required_approving_review_count // 0) >= 2)' 2>/dev/null) || s=false
[ "$p" = true ] || [ "$s" = true ] && echo compliant

remediation.command: Settings > Branches (or Rules > Rulesets) for the default branch: enable Require a pull request before merging with Required approvals = 2 (gh api -X PUT repos/<owner>/<repo>/branches/<branch>/protection ... required_approving_review_count=2), and require MFA for the organization.

title: Ensure all public repositories contain a SECURITY.md file
description: A SECURITY.md file is a security policy file that offers instruction on reporting security vulnerabilities in a project. When someone creates an issue within a specific project, a link to the SECURITY.md file will subsequently be shown. A SECURITY.md file provides users with crucial security information. It can also serve an important role in project maintenance, encouraging users to think ahead about how to properly handle potential security issues ... Every non-archived public repository of the organization must have SECURITY.md in the root, .github/ or docs/, unless the organization .github repository provides a default one. Uses the GitHub REST/GraphQL API through gh api (read-only). The repository comes from GH_REPO or the current git checkout (gh's {owner}/{repo} resolution, GH_HOST for GitHub Enterprise Server); the organization comes from GH_ORG (default: the repository owner). Fails when gh is missing or unauthenticated (gh auth login or GH_TOKEN); organization settings and branch protection need an owner/admin token.
reference: CIS GitHub Benchmark v1.2.0 - 1.2.1 Ensure all public repositories contain a SECURITY.md file

audit.command:
command -v gh >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1
gh auth status >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1
O=${GH_ORG:-$(gh api 'repos/{owner}/{repo}' --jq .owner.login 2>/dev/null)}
[ -n "$O" ] || exit 1
rs=$(gh api --paginate "orgs/$O/repos?type=public&per_page=100" --jq '.[] | select(.archived | not) | .full_name' 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
for f in SECURITY.md .github/SECURITY.md docs/SECURITY.md; do
  gh api "repos/$O/.github/contents/$f" --silent >/dev/null 2>&1 && { echo compliant; exit 0; }
done
bad=0
for r in $rs; do
  ok=0
  for f in SECURITY.md .github/SECURITY.md docs/SECURITY.md; do
    gh api "repos/$r/contents/$f" --silent >/dev/null 2>&1 && { ok=1; break; }
  done
  [ "$ok" -eq 1 ] || { echo "no SECURITY.md: $r"; bad=1; }
done
[ "$bad" -eq 0 ] && echo compliant

remediation.command: Add a SECURITY.md (root, .github/ or docs/) describing how to report vulnerabilities to each listed public repository, or once to the organization .github repository.
